claim: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) is an opportunistic, frequently multidrug-resistant pathogen that can cause severe infections in hospitalized patients.
source: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) is an opportunistic, frequently multidrug-resistant pathogen that can cause severe infections in hospitalized patients.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about PA's characteristics and clinical impact.

claim: Antibodies against the PA virulence factor, PcrV, protect from death and disease in a variety of animal models.
source: Antibodies against the PA virulence factor, PcrV, protect from death and disease in a variety of animal models.
evidence: This statement is supported by references to prior published work on PcrV antibodies in animal models.

claim: Clinical trials of PcrV-binding antibody-based products have thus far failed to demonstrate benefit.
source: However, clinical trials of PcrV-binding antibody-based products have thus far failed to demonstrate benefit.
evidence: This statement references known outcomes of clinical trials, which are cited elsewhere in the manuscript.

claim: Prior PcrV antibody candidates were derivations of antibodies identified using protein-immunized animal systems and required extensive engineering to optimize binding and/or reduce immunogenicity.
source: Prior candidates were derivations of antibodies identified using protein-immunized animal systems and required extensive engineering to optimize binding and/or reduce immunogenicity.
evidence: This statement describes the methodology used in prior antibody development efforts, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: PA infections are common in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF).
source: Of note, PA infections are common in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF), who are generally believed to mount normal adaptive immune responses.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about CF patients and PA infections.

claim: People with cystic fibrosis are generally believed to mount normal adaptive immune responses.
source: Of note, PA infections are common in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF), who are generally believed to mount normal adaptive immune responses.
evidence: This statement reflects established understanding about immune function in CF patients, supported by citations.

claim: The authors utilized a tetramer reagent to detect and isolate PcrV-specific B cells in pwCF.
source: Here, we utilized a tetramer reagent to detect and isolate PcrV-specific B cells in pwCF and, via single-cell sorting and paired-chain sequencing, identified the B cell receptor (BCR) variable region sequences that confer PcrV-specificity.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: The authors identified B cell receptor (BCR) variable region sequences that confer PcrV-specificity via single-cell sorting and paired-chain sequencing.
source: Here, we utilized a tetramer reagent to detect and isolate PcrV-specific B cells in pwCF and, via single-cell sorting and paired-chain sequencing, identified the B cell receptor (BCR) variable region sequences that confer PcrV-specificity.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach and results of the study.

claim: The authors derived multiple high affinity anti-PcrV monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from PcrV-specific B cells across three donors.
source: We derived multiple high affinity anti-PcrV monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from PcrV-specific B cells across three donors, including mAbs that exhibit potent anti-PA activity in a murine pneumonia model.
evidence: This statement summarizes the experimental results of antibody generation and characterization.

claim: Some of the derived mAbs exhibit potent anti-PA activity in a murine pneumonia model.
source: We derived multiple high affinity anti-PcrV monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) from PcrV-specific B cells across three donors, including mAbs that exhibit potent anti-PA activity in a murine pneumonia model.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vivo mouse studies presented in the manuscript.

claim: PA is a gram-negative bacteria responsible for significant morbidity and mortality in vulnerable individuals.
source: PA is a gram-negative bacteria responsible for significant morbidity and mortality in vulnerable individuals.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about PA's characteristics and clinical impact.

claim: Treatment of PA is challenging because of intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance to most antibiotic drug classes.
source: Treatment is challenging because of intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance to most antibiotic drug classes.
evidence: This reflects established clinical knowledge about PA antibiotic resistance.

claim: PA is one of the most common pathogens in severe healthcare-associated infections.
source: PA is one of the most common pathogens in severe healthcare-associated infections (Mancuso et al., 2021; Weiner-Lastinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by cited epidemiological studies.

claim: New anti-pseudomonal medicines are urgently needed due to significant mortality caused by multi-drug resistant strains and lack of alternative therapies.
source: Due to the significant mortality caused by multi-drug resistant strains and the lack of alternative therapies, new anti-pseudomonal medicines are urgently needed.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from established knowledge about PA resistance and treatment challenges.

claim: mAbs that bind to key PA virulence factors, such as PcrV, have shown promise in animal models.
source: mAbs that bind to key PA virulence factors, such as PcrV, have shown promise in animal models (Baer et al., 2009; Frank et al., 2002; Hotinger and May, 2020; Sawa et al., 2014; Simonis et al., 2023; Warrener et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple cited studies demonstrating efficacy in animal models.

claim: PcrV is a 28 kDa surface protein that forms the distal tip of the type III secretion system required for toxin injection into host cells.
source: PcrV is a 28 kDa surface protein that forms the distal tip of the type III secretion system required for toxin injection into host cells (Sato and Frank, 2011).
evidence: This is established structural and functional knowledge about PcrV, supported by citation.

claim: The authors' groups have previously generated potent anti-pathogen mAbs by sequencing the variable regions of the BCR derived from antigen-specific memory B cells (MBCs) that arise following natural infection in humans for COVID-19 and malaria.
source: In prior studies of COVID-19 and malaria, our groups have generated potent anti-pathogen mAbs by sequencing the variable regions of the BCR derived from antigen-specific memory B cells (MBCs) that arise following natural infection in humans (Hale et al., 2022; Rodda et al., 2021; Thouvenel et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement references prior work by the authors, supported by citations to their previous publications.

claim: The authors hypothesized that protective anti-PcrV monoclonal antibodies could be derived from B cells in individuals previously infected with PA.
source: Therefore, we hypothesized that protective anti-PcrV monoclonal antibodies could be derived from B cells in individuals previously infected with PA.
evidence: This is a stated hypothesis based on prior work and reasoning.

claim: People with cystic fibrosis experience intermittent or chronic airway PA infections.
source: People with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) experience intermittent or chronic airway PA infections (Cramer et al., 2023; Lund-Palau et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about CF patients, supported by citations.

claim: Intermittent PA infections early in childhood in CF patients eventually progress to a state of persistent, chronic airway colonization.
source: Intermittent infections early in childhood eventually progress to a state of persistent, chronic airway colonization.
evidence: This describes the natural history of PA infection in CF patients, based on established clinical knowledge.

claim: CF is a multi-organ disease caused by mutations in the gene encoding cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR).
source: CF is a multi-organ disease caused by mutations in the gene encoding cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR), an apical epithelial ion channel involved in chloride and bicarbonate transport (Shteinberg et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genetic basis of CF, supported by citation.

claim: CFTR is an apical epithelial ion channel involved in chloride and bicarbonate transport.
source: CF is a multi-organ disease caused by mutations in the gene encoding cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR), an apical epithelial ion channel involved in chloride and bicarbonate transport (Shteinberg et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the function of CFTR, based on established knowledge and citation.

claim: Several mechanisms related to the biology of the CF airway have been proposed to explain susceptibility to PA.
source: Several mechanisms related to the biology of the CF airway have been proposed to explain susceptibility to PA (Rossi et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement references proposed mechanisms in the literature, supported by citation.

claim: pwCF do not have intrinsic deficits in adaptive immunity.
source: Importantly, pwCF do not have intrinsic deficits in adaptive immunity (Alicandro et al., 2023; Ong and Ramsey, 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by cited studies on immune function in CF patients.

claim: Class-switched anti-PcrV antibodies are present in CF serum and sputum, at higher concentrations than the general population.
source: Class-switched anti-PcrV antibodies are present in CF serum and sputum, at higher concentrations than the general population (Mauch and Levy, 2014; Moss et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by cited studies measuring antibody levels in CF patients.

claim: The PcrV-specific B cells that give rise to antibody-secreting cells had not been previously studied.
source: However, the PcrV-specific B cells that give rise to antibody-secreting cells had not been previously studied.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in prior research based on literature review.

claim: pwCF have more PcrV-specific circulating B cells compared to non-CF controls.
source: Here, we show that pwCF have more PcrV-specific circulating B cells compared to non-CF controls.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and 1C comparing CF and non-CF donors.

claim: The authors utilized single-cell sequencing to identify PcrV-specific paired-chain BCR sequences in pwCF.
source: Building on this finding, we utilized single-cell sequencing to identify PcrV-specific paired-chain BCR sequences in pwCF.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: The authors generated novel anti-PcrV mAbs from BCR sequences derived from PcrV-specific B cells and MBCs.
source: From BCR sequences derived from PcrV-specific B cells and MBCs, we generated novel anti-PcrV mAbs, including several that confer robust protection against a virulent strain of PA in an in vivo pneumonia challenge model.
evidence: This summarizes the experimental results of the study.

claim: Several of the generated mAbs confer robust protection against a virulent strain of PA in an in vivo pneumonia challenge model.
source: From BCR sequences derived from PcrV-specific B cells and MBCs, we generated novel anti-PcrV mAbs, including several that confer robust protection against a virulent strain of PA in an in vivo pneumonia challenge model.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mouse pneumonia challenge studies shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: The authors previously described techniques to generate fluorophore-linked tetramers to isolate antigen-specific B cells.
source: We previously described techniques to generate a fluorophore-linked tetramers to isolate antigen-specific B cells (Krishnamurty et al., 2016).
evidence: This references prior methodology developed by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: The authors generated a tetramer using recombinant PcrV protein to identify PcrV-specific B cells.
source: To identify PcrV-specific B cells, we generated a tetramer using recombinant PcrV protein.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: The authors generated a decoy tetramer consisting of irrelevant proteins linked to a tandem fluorophore.
source: In parallel, we also generated a decoy tetramer consisting of irrelevant proteins linked to a tandem fluorophore (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Immunization of C57BL/6 mice with 250 µg purified, recombinant PcrV protein resuspended in Sigma Adjuvant System induced an expanded population of class-switched PcrV+ B cells on day 7.
source: To test the tetramer reagent, we immunized C57BL/6 mice with 250 µg purified, recombinant PcrV protein resuspended in Sigma Adjuvant System (SAS, Sigma). Immunization induced an expanded population of class-switched PcrV+ B cells on day 7, demonstrating the specificity of the reagent (Taylor et al., 2012; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mouse immunization studies shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mouse immunization experiment demonstrated the specificity of the PcrV tetramer reagent.
source: Immunization induced an expanded population of class-switched PcrV+ B cells on day 7, demonstrating the specificity of the reagent (Taylor et al., 2012; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The authors obtained peripheral blood samples from a cohort of 14 young adults with CF who were followed in CF clinic at Seattle Children's Hospital.
source: We next obtained peripheral blood samples from a cohort of 14 young adults with CF who were followed in CF clinic at Seattle Children's Hospital.
evidence: This describes the study population and sample collection.

claim: B cells specific for any single antigen are rare.
source: As B cells specific for any single antigen are rare, tetramer-bound cells were enriched on an anti-fluorophore magnetic column prior to analysis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about B cell frequencies that informed the experimental design.

claim: After enrichment, PcrV-specific cells made up ≥5% of B cells in 10 out of 14 (71%) of CF donors.
source: After enrichment, PcrV-specific cells made up ≥5% of B cells in 10 out of 14 (71%) of CF donors and demonstrated significant expansion in cell number over non-CF individuals (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PcrV-specific B cells demonstrated significant expansion in cell number in CF donors over non-CF individuals.
source: After enrichment, PcrV-specific cells made up ≥5% of B cells in 10 out of 14 (71%) of CF donors and demonstrated significant expansion in cell number over non-CF individuals (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Similar differences between CF vs. non-CF donors were found when the number of PcrV-specific B cells in each sample was normalized to lymphocyte count.
source: Similar differences between CF vs. non-CF donors were found when the number of PcrV-specific B cells in each sample was normalized to lymphocyte count (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PBMCs were isolated from a blood sample from CF Donor 1, who was chronically infected with PA based on at least 2 PA + oropharyngeal cultures in three consecutive years collected as part of routine care.
source: PBMCs were isolated from a blood sample from a CF donor (Donor 1), who was chronically infected with PA based on at least 2 PA + oropharyngeal cultures in three consecutive years collected as part of routine care (Green et al., 2012; Mogayzel et al., 2014; Rosenfeld et al., 2022) (see Table 1 for clinical characteristics).
evidence: This describes the clinical characteristics of the study subject, with definition supported by citations.

claim: Only two PcrV-specific B cells sequenced in Donor 1 expressed the canonical MBC surface markers (CD21+CD27+).
source: Interestingly, only two PcrV-specific B cells sequenced in Donor 1 expressed the canonical MBC surface markers (CD21+CD27+) (gating strategy shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: BCR sequencing of PcrV-specific B cells from Donor 1 revealed predominantly germline sequences with little or no evidence for somatic hypermutation.
source: Consistent with these observations, BCR sequencing of PcrV-specific B cells revealed predominantly germline sequences with little or no evidence for somatic hypermutation (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The authors generated mAbs that employed the BCR variable regions from 10 tetramer-bound B cells isolated from Donor 1.
source: We next generated mAbs that employed the BCR variable regions from 10 tetramer-bound B cells isolated from Donor 1.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for antibody generation.

claim: The surface-expressed isotype of all PcrV-specific B cells from Donor 1 was IgM.
source: As the surface-expressed isotype of all these PcrV-specific B cells was IgM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), we first expressed the BCR sequences as pentameric IgM antibodies.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Supernatants from cells co-transfected with heavy, light, and J chain plasmids exhibited strong binding to PcrV for 3 of 10 CF-derived BCRs (denoted BCRs 408, 411, and 421).
source: When tested for binding to recombinant PcrV in a plate-bound ELISA assay, supernatants collected from cells co-transfected with heavy, light, and J chain plasmids (to make pentameric IgM) exhibited strong binding to PcrV for 3 of 10 CF-derived BCRs (denoted BCRs 408, 411, and 421) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The light chain for BCR 421 contains several mutations in CDR1.
source: The light chain for BCR 421 contains several mutations in CDR1.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of the BCR.

claim: mAbs from clones 408 and 411 had high affinity as measured by ELISA despite having germline sequences.
source: Despite having germline sequences, mAbs from clones 408 and 411 had high affinity as measured by ELISA.
evidence: This is based on ELISA binding data and sequence analysis.

claim: For mAbs that target divergent pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2 and Plasmodium falciparum, multimerized antibodies (eg. pentameric IgM) have enhanced binding and protection properties in vitro.
source: We have previously found that for mAbs that target divergent pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2 and Plasmodium falciparum, multimerized antibodies (eg. pentameric IgM) have enhanced binding and protection properties in vitro (Hale et al., 2022; Thouvenel et al., 2021).
evidence: This references prior findings by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: Nearly all current monoclonal antibody therapeutics employ the IgG1 isotype.
source: However, nearly all current monoclonal antibody therapeutics employ the IgG1 isotype (McConnell, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about therapeutic antibody development, supported by citation.

claim: CF BCRs 408 and 411 exhibited binding to PcrV as both IgM and IgG mAbs.
source: CF BCRs 408 and 411 exhibited binding to PcrV as both IgM and IgG mAbs; with higher binding as IgM, reflecting the avidity of IgM multimers (Hale et al., 2022; Thouvenel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: CF BCRs 408 and 411 exhibited higher binding to PcrV as IgM compared to IgG, reflecting the avidity of IgM multimers.
source: CF BCRs 408 and 411 exhibited binding to PcrV as both IgM and IgG mAbs; with higher binding as IgM, reflecting the avidity of IgM multimers (Hale et al., 2022; Thouvenel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2C and interpretation based on known properties of IgM.

claim: V2L2MD is a heavily engineered anti-PcrV mAb that was generated by phage display binding optimization from a precursor candidate identified by hybridoma screening from PcrV-immunized, human-variable region transgenic mice.
source: V2L2MD is a heavily engineered anti-PcrV mAb that was generated by phage display binding optimization from a precursor candidate identified by hybridoma screening from PcrV-immunized, human-variable region transgenic mice (Warrener et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the origin and development of V2L2MD, supported by citation.

claim: Gremubamab consists of the paired heavy and light chain variable regions of V2L2MD fused to an anti-polysaccharide (Psl) single chain variable fragment (scFv) and the human IgG1 constant region.
source: The clinical candidate bi-specific, gremubamab, consists of the paired heavy and light chain variable regions of V2L2MD fused to an anti-polysaccharide (Psl) single chain variable fragment (scFv) and the human IgG1 constant region (Chastre et al., 2022; DiGiandomenico et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the structure of gremubamab, supported by citations.

claim: As IgM mAbs, 411 and V2L2MD exhibited similar binding to PcrV, on par with the commercially-sourced gremubamab.
source: As IgM mAbs, 411 and V2L2MD exhibited similar binding to PcrV, on par with the commercially-sourced gremubamab.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Mice treated with a single, 20 µg intranasal dose of anti-PcrV IgG (408 and 411) exhibited an ~2 log reduction in burden of bacteria in the lungs at 24 hr in comparison with an off-target control mAb or vehicle (PBS) only.
source: Mice treated with a single, 20 µg intranasal dose of anti-PcrV IgG (408 and 411) exhibited an ~2 log reduction in burden of bacteria in the lungs at 24 hr in comparison with an off-target control mAb or vehicle (PBS) only (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mouse pneumonia challenge studies shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The CF-derived mAbs 408 and 411 performed equivalently to the positive control V2L2MD mAb in the mouse pneumonia challenge model.
source: The CF-derived mAbs performed equivalently to the positive control V2L2MD mAb.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B comparing the performance of different mAbs.

claim: Isolation of PcrV-specific B cells from a chronically infected CF donor enabled the rapid discovery of two protective mAbs.
source: The above findings demonstrate that isolation of PcrV-specific B cells from a chronically infected CF donor enabled the rapid discovery of two protective mAbs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results presented.

claim: In earlier studies of other pathogens, antigen-specific MBCs had been excellent sources for high-affinity, protective BCR sequences.
source: In our earlier studies of other pathogens, antigen-specific MBCs had been excellent sources for high-affinity, protective BCR sequences (Rodda et al., 2021; Thouvenel et al., 2021).
evidence: This references prior findings by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: The authors hypothesized that higher affinity, anti-PcrV mAb might be isolated from antigen-experienced, somatically hypermutated, PcrV-specific MBCs.
source: Therefore, we hypothesized that higher affinity, anti-PcrV mAb might be isolated from antigen-experienced, somatically hypermutated, PcrV-specific MBCs.
evidence: This is a stated hypothesis based on prior work and reasoning.

claim: Donor 2 had tested culture positive for PA for the first time 6 mo prior to sample collection and was negative on most recent testing.
source: We obtained peripheral blood samples from two additional pwCF: Donor 2, who had tested culture positive for PA for the first time 6 mo prior to sample collection and was negative on most recent testing, and Donor 3, who like Donor 1, was considered to be chronically infected at the time of blood sample (Table 1; Green et al., 2012; Rosenfeld et al., 2022).
evidence: This describes the clinical characteristics of the study subject.

claim: Donor 3 was considered to be chronically infected with PA at the time of blood sample.
source: We obtained peripheral blood samples from two additional pwCF: Donor 2, who had tested culture positive for PA for the first time 6 mo prior to sample collection and was negative on most recent testing, and Donor 3, who like Donor 1, was considered to be chronically infected at the time of blood sample (Table 1; Green et al., 2012; Rosenfeld et al., 2022).
evidence: This describes the clinical characteristics of the study subject.

claim: Sequences derived from PcrV-specific cells identified by surface phenotype as likely MBCs (CD21+CD27+) carried an average somatic hypermutation load of 2.5% in Donor 2.
source: Sequences derived from PcrV-specific cells identified by surface phenotype as likely MBCs (CD21+CD27+) carried an average somatic hypermutation load of 2.5% in Donor 2 (Figure 4A) and <1% in Donor 3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Sequences derived from PcrV-specific cells identified by surface phenotype as likely MBCs (CD21+CD27+) carried an average somatic hypermutation load of <1% in Donor 3.
source: Sequences derived from PcrV-specific cells identified by surface phenotype as likely MBCs (CD21+CD27+) carried an average somatic hypermutation load of 2.5% in Donor 2 (Figure 4A) and <1% in Donor 3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There was significant breadth in V gene usage within and between donors.
source: There was significant breadth in V gene usage within and between donors (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: IGHV3-23 is used, with mutations, in the V2L2MD antibody.
source: The heavy chain IGHV3-23 is used, with mutations, in the V2L2MD antibody, and is a very common VH gene segment in most human B cell repertoire studies (Rubelt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on known sequence information about V2L2MD and general knowledge about B cell repertoires, supported by citation.

claim: IGHV3-23 is a very common VH gene segment in most human B cell repertoire studies.
source: The heavy chain IGHV3-23 is used, with mutations, in the V2L2MD antibody, and is a very common VH gene segment in most human B cell repertoire studies (Rubelt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about B cell repertoires, supported by citation.

claim: IGHV3-23 was well represented in the dataset of PcrV-specific B cells from CF donors.
source: Accordingly, IGHV3-23 was also well represented in this dataset.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the sequencing data.

claim: None of the PcrV-specific B cells sequenced for the study paired VH3-23 heavy chains with IGKV1-6, the V2L2MD light chain variable gene.
source: Notably, none of the PcrV-specific B cells sequenced for our study paired VH3-23 heavy chains with IGKV1-6, the V2L2MD light chain variable gene (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), and IGKV1-6 was infrequent in our dataset.
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: IGKV1-6 was infrequent in the dataset of PcrV-specific B cells from CF donors.
source: Notably, none of the PcrV-specific B cells sequenced for our study paired VH3-23 heavy chains with IGKV1-6, the V2L2MD light chain variable gene (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), and IGKV1-6 was infrequent in our dataset.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the sequencing data.

claim: 12 BCRs from MBCs were randomly selected for cloning into IgG1 expression plasmids.
source: To pursue our goal of identifying potential protective mAbs among MBCs, 12 of these BCRs were randomly selected for cloning into IgG1 expression plasmids.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for antibody generation.

claim: BCRs 435 and 442 were the most striking binders in the transfection screen.
source: BCRs 435 and 442 were the most striking binders in the transfection screen.
evidence: This is based on ELISA screening data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The raw heavy chain sequence that became BCR clone 439 included the IGHA constant region that defines the IgA antibody isotype.
source: Based on performance in the screen or for reasons of special interest (for example, the raw heavy chain sequence that became BCR clone 439 included the IGHA constant region that defines the IgA antibody isotype, the predominant isotype in respiratory secretions), 5 MBC-derived BCRs were chosen for production as purified IgG mAbs.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of the BCR.

claim: IgA is the predominant isotype in respiratory secretions.
source: Based on performance in the screen or for reasons of special interest (for example, the raw heavy chain sequence that became BCR clone 439 included the IGHA constant region that defines the IgA antibody isotype, the predominant isotype in respiratory secretions), 5 MBC-derived BCRs were chosen for production as purified IgG mAbs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about antibody isotypes in mucosal immunity.

claim: 2 of 5 MBC-derived mAbs matched or exceeded PcrV binding exhibited by the protective, donor 1 mAb, 411.
source: When this panel of purified mAbs was evaluated at matched concentrations (Figure 4C), 2 of 5 of MBC-derived mAbs matched or exceeded PcrV binding exhibited by the protective, donor 1 mAb, 411.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 4 of 5 MBC-derived mAbs matched or exceeded the PcrV binding of the protective donor-1 derived mAb, 408 IgG.
source: Furthermore, 4 of 5 matched or exceeded the other protective donor-1 derived protective mAb, 408 IgG.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: All three CF MBC-derived mAbs (437, 439, and 442) achieved significant reductions in bacterial burden at 24 hr when compared to an off-target control mAb or saline alone.
source: Strikingly, all three CF MBC-derived mAbs including 437 (originally derived from an IgG MBC), 439 (derived from an IgA MBC), and 442 (derived from an IgM MBC) achieved significant reductions in bacterial burden at 24 hr when compared to an off-target control mAb or saline alone (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mouse pneumonia challenge studies shown in Figure 5.

claim: mAb 437 was originally derived from an IgG MBC.
source: Strikingly, all three CF MBC-derived mAbs including 437 (originally derived from an IgG MBC), 439 (derived from an IgA MBC), and 442 (derived from an IgM MBC) achieved significant reductions in bacterial burden at 24 hr when compared to an off-target control mAb or saline alone (Figure 5).
evidence: This describes the origin of the mAb based on the surface phenotype of the B cell from which it was derived.

claim: mAb 439 was derived from an IgA MBC.
source: Strikingly, all three CF MBC-derived mAbs including 437 (originally derived from an IgG MBC), 439 (derived from an IgA MBC), and 442 (derived from an IgM MBC) achieved significant reductions in bacterial burden at 24 hr when compared to an off-target control mAb or saline alone (Figure 5).
evidence: This describes the origin of the mAb based on the surface phenotype of the B cell from which it was derived.

claim: mAb 442 was derived from an IgM MBC.
source: Strikingly, all three CF MBC-derived mAbs including 437 (originally derived from an IgG MBC), 439 (derived from an IgA MBC), and 442 (derived from an IgM MBC) achieved significant reductions in bacterial burden at 24 hr when compared to an off-target control mAb or saline alone (Figure 5).
evidence: This describes the origin of the mAb based on the surface phenotype of the B cell from which it was derived.

claim: The authors obtained 175 unique paired heavy-light chain BCR sequences of PcrV-binding B cells from 3 donors with CF.
source: In summary, we obtained 175 unique paired heavy-light chain BCR sequences of PcrV-binding B cells from 3 donors with CF.
evidence: This summarizes the sequencing results from the study.

claim: After expressing 20 BCRs as human mAbs, at least moderate in vitro PcrV binding was confirmed for 12 of 20 (60%).
source: After expressing 20 BCRs as human mAbs, we confirmed at least moderate in vitro PcrV binding for the majority screened (12 of 20, 60%), and high-affinity binding for 7 (35%).
evidence: This summarizes the binding results from ELISA screening.

claim: High-affinity PcrV binding was confirmed for 7 of 20 (35%) expressed BCRs.
source: After expressing 20 BCRs as human mAbs, we confirmed at least moderate in vitro PcrV binding for the majority screened (12 of 20, 60%), and high-affinity binding for 7 (35%).
evidence: This summarizes the binding results from ELISA screening.

claim: Of the 5 mAbs tested in an established in vivo model of PA pneumonia, all produced significant reductions in lung bacterial burden.
source: Of the 5 mAbs tested in an established in vivo model of PA pneumonia, all produced significant reductions in lung bacterial burden.
evidence: This summarizes the in vivo protection results shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: The authors' approach was more efficient compared to standard methods for antibody discovery using immunized mice and screening hundreds to thousands of hybridomas.
source: In comparison to standard methods for antibody discovery using immunized mice and screening hundreds to thousands of hybridomas, our approach was more efficient.
evidence: This is a comparative assessment based on the number of candidates screened versus protective antibodies identified.

claim: The results reveal a diverse PcrV-specific repertoire for PA-specific B cells in pwCF.
source: In addition, our results reveal a diverse PcrV-specific repertoire for PA-specific B cells in pwCF.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the sequencing data showing breadth in V gene usage.

claim: Relative to the projected need for new antimicrobials, few novel antimicrobials are under active pharmaceutical development.
source: Unfortunately, relative to the projected need, few novel antimicrobials are under active pharmaceutical development (Theuretzbacher et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation discussing the antimicrobial development pipeline.

claim: Antibacterial mAbs could fill the widening gap as alternatives, or adjuncts, to traditional antibiotics.
source: Antibacterial mAbs could fill the widening gap as alternatives, or adjuncts, to traditional antibiotics.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential role of antibacterial mAbs.

claim: Mechanisms of intrinsic resistance already limit therapeutic options for multidrug-resistant PA.
source: Because mechanisms of intrinsic resistance already limit therapeutic options, multidrug-resistant PA is especially difficult to treat (Yaeger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: Multidrug-resistant PA is especially difficult to treat.
source: Because mechanisms of intrinsic resistance already limit therapeutic options, multidrug-resistant PA is especially difficult to treat (Yaeger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge, supported by citation.

claim: Efforts to develop mAbs targeting PcrV are bolstered by strong evidence for antibody-mediated protection in animal models.
source: Efforts to develop mAbs targeting PcrV, a critical component of the PA toxin injection apparatus, are bolstered by strong evidence for antibody-mediated protection in animal models (Goure et al., 2005; Moriyama et al., 2009; Sawa et al., 1999; Sécher et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to animal model studies.

claim: Two engineered antibody-like drug candidates (a Fab fragment and a bi-specific mAb) derived from mice failed to achieve efficacy in human trials.
source: Unfortunately, two engineered antibody-like drug candidates (a Fab fragment and a bi-specific mAb) derived from mice failed to achieve efficacy in human trials (Chastre et al., 2022; François et al., 2012; Jain et al., 2018; Yaeger et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to clinical trial reports.

claim: New approaches are needed to identify fully human mAbs with robust anti-PA protective activity, reduced immunogenicity, and improved pharmacokinetics.
source: New approaches are needed to identify fully human mAbs with robust anti-PA protective activity, reduced immunogenicity, and improved pharmacokinetics.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the failure of prior approaches and known limitations of animal-derived antibodies.

claim: Traditional methods of mAb development begin with immunization of mice with a recombinant protein.
source: Traditional methods of mAb development begin with immunization of mice with a recombinant protein.
evidence: This is established knowledge about traditional antibody development methods.

claim: To address the immunogenicity of the murine constant region, mouse-derived antibodies must be iteratively re-humanized in vitro and/or modified into antibody fragments (Fab) which lack effector functions and are subject to rapid renal clearance.
source: To address the immunogenicity of the murine constant region, mouse-derived antibodies must then be iteratively re-humanized in vitro and/or modified into antibody fragments (Fab) which lack effector functions and are subject to rapid renal clearance.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the limitations of mouse-derived antibodies and approaches to address them.

claim: Fully in vitro strategies like phage display can enable the use of human variable domains.
source: Although fully in vitro strategies like phage display can enable the use of human variable domains (Tavernier et al., 2016; DiGiandomenico et al., 2012), the high-throughput screening processes are vulnerable to bottleneck effects and drift, and lack key features of in vivo B cell development, such as selection against autoreactivity.
evidence: This is established knowledge about phage display technology, supported by citations.

claim: High-throughput screening processes in phage display are vulnerable to bottleneck effects and drift, and lack key features of in vivo B cell development, such as selection against autoreactivity.
source: Although fully in vitro strategies like phage display can enable the use of human variable domains (Tavernier et al., 2016; DiGiandomenico et al., 2012), the high-throughput screening processes are vulnerable to bottleneck effects and drift, and lack key features of in vivo B cell development, such as selection against autoreactivity.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of phage display limitations based on knowledge of B cell biology.

claim: The authors generated multiple anti-PcrV mAbs directly from the BCR variable regions of antigen-specific B cells derived from CF donors with intermittent (past) or persistent Pa infection.
source: Here, we generated multiple anti-PcrV mAbs directly from the BCR variable regions of antigen-specific B cells derived from CF donors with intermittent (past) or persistent Pa infection.
evidence: This summarizes the experimental approach and results of the study.

claim: The antibody discovery strategy was extremely efficient, requiring expression of very few (<12) BCRs to yield protective anti-pseudomonal mAbs.
source: However, our antibody discovery strategy was extremely efficient, requiring expression of very few (<12) BCRs to yield protective anti-pseudomonal mAbs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results showing high success rate.

claim: In in vivo challenge studies, 4 of 5 mAbs directly cloned from human B cells achieved control of PA.
source: Strikingly, in in vivo challenge studies, 4 of 5 mAbs directly cloned from human B cells achieved control of PA.
evidence: This summarizes the in vivo protection results from the study.

claim: Doses achieving similar reductions in lung bacterial burdens have resulted in 100% survival in cohorts of mice in prior studies of V2L2MD.
source: While assessment of lung bacterial burden requires sacrifice of the treated mice, doses achieving similar reductions in lung bacterial burdens have resulted in 100% survival in cohorts of mice in prior studies of V2L2MD (Warrener et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement references prior published results, supported by citation.

claim: The findings employing BCR sequences from multiple isotypes are consistent with contemporaneous work by Simonis et al., 2023 showing protection in neutropenic mice by three anti-PcrV mAbs discovered by single-cell BCR sequencing of IgG-expressing B cells from two CF donors.
source: Our findings employing BCR sequences from multiple isotypes are consistent with contemporaneous work by Simonis et al., 2023 showing protection in neutropenic mice by three anti-PcrV mAbs discovered by single-cell BCR sequencing of IgG-expressing B cells from two CF donors.
evidence: This statement compares the current findings to a contemporaneous study, supported by citation.

claim: The anti-PcrV mAbs isolated using the authors' approach matched the in vivo performance of V2L2MD IgG.
source: Notably, the anti-PcrV mAbs antibodies isolated using our approach matched the in vivo performance of V2L2MD IgG, the highly engineered PcrV-specific binding component of the clinical bi-specific antibody, gremubamab.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the in vivo protection data for different mAbs.

claim: The anti-PcrV antibody (V2L2MD) was effective in animal models.
source: The anti-PcrV antibody (V2L2MD) was effective in animal models, but the bi-specific antibody containing this anti-PcrV binding moiety failed to achieve the targeted efficacy outcomes in Phase 2 (Chastre et al., 2022; DiGiandomenico et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to preclinical and clinical studies.

claim: The bi-specific antibody containing the V2L2MD anti-PcrV binding moiety failed to achieve the targeted efficacy outcomes in Phase 2 clinical trials.
source: The anti-PcrV antibody (V2L2MD) was effective in animal models, but the bi-specific antibody containing this anti-PcrV binding moiety failed to achieve the targeted efficacy outcomes in Phase 2 (Chastre et al., 2022; DiGiandomenico et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to clinical trial reports.

claim: mAbs derived directly from human B cells have potential theoretical advantages in human use.
source: Importantly, mAbs derived directly from human B cells have potential theoretical advantages in human use.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential advantages based on reasoning.

claim: Compared to animal-derived anti-pseudomonal candidates like gremubamab, human MBC-derived mAbs are expected to exhibit reduced immunogenicity and manifest fully human effector functions.
source: Compared to animal-derived anti-pseudomonal candidates like gremubamab, human MBC-derived mAbs are expected to exhibit reduced immunogenicity Strand et al., 2017 and manifest fully human effector functions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about expected advantages, partially supported by citation.

claim: Whether human MBC-derived antibodies will be more effective in the clinical setting remains to be determined.
source: Whether such antibodies will be more effective in the clinical setting, however, remains to be determined.
evidence: This acknowledges uncertainty about clinical efficacy.

claim: The goal of this study was to generate novel protective mAbs for potential therapeutic use.
source: While the goal of this study was to generate novel protective mAbs for potential therapeutic use, our findings also offer new insight into the cellular sources of the humoral response to PA in pwCF, expanding on studies which have thus far been limited to the measurement of secreted antibodies (Mauch and Levy, 2014).
evidence: This states the primary objective of the study.

claim: The findings offer new insight into the cellular sources of the humoral response to PA in pwCF, expanding on studies which have thus far been limited to the measurement of secreted antibodies.
source: While the goal of this study was to generate novel protective mAbs for potential therapeutic use, our findings also offer new insight into the cellular sources of the humoral response to PA in pwCF, expanding on studies which have thus far been limited to the measurement of secreted antibodies (Mauch and Levy, 2014).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study results in the context of prior work, supported by citation.

claim: Circulating PcrV-specific B cells in CF individuals were expanded compared to non-CF individuals.
source: As we hypothesized, given the uniquely high frequency of PA infections in the CF population, circulating PcrV-specific B cells in CF individuals were expanded compared to non-CF individuals.
evidence: This summarizes the experimental findings comparing CF and non-CF donors.

claim: The ability to generate protective mAbs ex vivo from CF B cells demonstrates that B cells with the technical capacity to produce functional anti-PA antibodies are present in the peripheral blood.
source: While the ability to generate protective mAbs ex vivo from CF B cells demonstrates that B cells with the technical capacity to produce functional anti-PA antibodies are present in the peripheral blood, and recent work has shown that anti-PcrV antibodies capable of neutralizing PA in vitro are present in some pwCF (Simonis et al., 2023), multiple in vivo challenges may limit PA clearance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful generation of protective mAbs from CF B cells.

claim: Recent work has shown that anti-PcrV antibodies capable of neutralizing PA in vitro are present in some pwCF.
source: While the ability to generate protective mAbs ex vivo from CF B cells demonstrates that B cells with the technical capacity to produce functional anti-PA antibodies are present in the peripheral blood, and recent work has shown that anti-PcrV antibodies capable of neutralizing PA in vitro are present in some pwCF (Simonis et al., 2023), multiple in vivo challenges may limit PA clearance.
evidence: This statement references recent findings, supported by citation.

claim: Multiple in vivo challenges may limit PA clearance in CF patients.
source: While the ability to generate protective mAbs ex vivo from CF B cells demonstrates that B cells with the technical capacity to produce functional anti-PA antibodies are present in the peripheral blood, and recent work has shown that anti-PcrV antibodies capable of neutralizing PA in vitro are present in some pwCF (Simonis et al., 2023), multiple in vivo challenges may limit PA clearance.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential limitations to PA clearance in vivo.

claim: Significant future work will be required to fully characterize the nature and dynamics of PA-specific B cells in CF individuals.
source: Significant future work will be required to fully characterize the nature and dynamics of PA-specific B cells in CF individuals.
evidence: This acknowledges limitations and future research needs.

claim: Better understanding of the endogenous anti-PA response might reveal insight that could enhance future therapeutic antibody products, enabling optimization of isotype, glycosylation, delivery site, or other features.
source: Better understanding of the endogenous anti-PA response might also reveal insight that could enhance future therapeutic antibody products, enabling optimization of isotype, glycosylation, delivery site, or other features.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications of research findings.

claim: The authors have previously shown that protective mAbs may be built from antigen-specific MBCs that target the parasite Plasmodium falciparum and the virus SARS-CoV-2.
source: We have previously shown that protective mAbs may be built from antigen-specific MBCs that target the parasite Plasmodium falciparum and the virus SARS-CoV-2 (Hale et al., 2022; Rodda et al., 2021; Thouvenel et al., 2021).
evidence: This references prior work by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: Human MBC-derived mAbs eliminate the humanization requirement and concern for residual immunogenicity.
source: Besides eliminating the humanization requirement and concern for residual immunogenicity, human MBC-derived mAbs are the product of evolved B cell development and maturation processes that encompass tremendous diversity and include selection against auto-reactivity and, for cells that have exited GCs, pre-optimized binding to antigen via affinity maturation.
evidence: This is a statement about advantages of human MBC-derived mAbs based on knowledge of B cell biology.

claim: Human MBC-derived mAbs are the product of evolved B cell development and maturation processes that encompass tremendous diversity and include selection against auto-reactivity.
source: Besides eliminating the humanization requirement and concern for residual immunogenicity, human MBC-derived mAbs are the product of evolved B cell development and maturation processes that encompass tremendous diversity and include selection against auto-reactivity and, for cells that have exited GCs, pre-optimized binding to antigen via affinity maturation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of B cell biology and development.

claim: For MBCs that have exited germinal centers, binding to antigen is pre-optimized via affinity maturation.
source: Besides eliminating the humanization requirement and concern for residual immunogenicity, human MBC-derived mAbs are the product of evolved B cell development and maturation processes that encompass tremendous diversity and include selection against auto-reactivity and, for cells that have exited GCs, pre-optimized binding to antigen via affinity maturation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of germinal center biology and affinity maturation.

claim: When combined with the results of the present study, human antigen-specific B cells may be broadly considered as an underutilized high-yield resource in the critical endeavor to discover new treatments for infectious diseases.
source: When combined with the results of our present study, human antigen-specific B cells may be broadly considered as an underutilized high-yield resource in the critical endeavor to discover new treatments for infectious diseases.
evidence: This is a broad conclusion drawn from the current study and prior work by the authors.
